traits_applied: abstraction low; literal concrete depiction over symbolic encoding
label complexity low; short plain-language labels only
first-read relation must be understandable without reading a legend at all -- no legend used
cap comparison at 2 dimensions with plain-language labels and no abstract scale (visual-analytical-graphic.json audience_adaptation.child-upper-elementary)

semantic_spec.question: Did the thing that would scare people (companies failing to pay back loans) get worse, or did only the government borrowing rate stay high?
must_communicate: US government borrowing rate stayed about the same and high between 9/1 and 9/5
the 'worry about companies failing' measure (credit spread) barely moved over the same window
these are two different things, and only one of them is a warning sign
must_not_include: a numeric axis or scale the reader must read to understand the comparison
the term 'OAS' or 'term premium' as a label inside the artwork

adjacent_representation.summary: The draft's 'is this a danger sign?' section explains in words that the borrowing rate stayed high while the worry-about-companies-failing measure barely moved.

redundancy_test.q1_new_perception: A 10-12 year old can see two bar heights side by side and immediately grasp 'one thing changed a lot, the other barely changed' without parsing two paragraphs of percentages.
redundancy_test.q2_harder_without_it: Without the bars, the reader has to hold four numbers (4.80%, 4.76-4.78%, ~1%, 1.01-1.03%) in mind and compare their sizes mentally -- exactly the abstraction step this audience profile says not to assume.
